title: Trump Effort to Prove Rampant Noncitizen Voting Leads to Few Charges So Far
partialText: Just 236 people have been charged with voting-fraud-related offenses by the Trump administration, despite its unsubstantiated claims that fraud is widespread.

title: Trump Says U.S. to End $4 Billion in Aid to Israel at End of Year
partialText: The president’s announcement on Election Day, which he said was part of an agreement reached months ago, was a sign of how quickly the politics surrounding Israel have shifted.

title: Israeli Claims of Iranian Chemical Weapons Divide U.S. Officials
partialText: Some administration officials suggested Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is trying to draw President Trump back into military action.

title: A Test for Israeli Democracy: Should Jews Ask Arabs to Join the Government?
partialText: Arab lawmakers give opponents of Benjamin Netanyahu a clear majority in the Parliament. But many Jewish lawmakers are trying to avoid relying on them.

title: Investigators Looking for Cause of Learjet Crash Say Ice Was ‘Certainly a Factor’
partialText: Ice, experts said, can change the shape of a plane’s wing, disrupting its aerodynamics.

title: Flouting Consumer Law, Insurers Refuse to Pay Medical Bills for Emergency Care
partialText: A law to end surprise medical bills has generated millions of high-dollar payouts for doctors. Health plans are now fighting back by frequently withholding money.

title: Strike on Ukraine Humanitarian Hub Is Feared to Be Among War’s Deadliest
partialText: Hours after the Russian attack, which killed at least 31 and left dozens missing, the United States said that peace talks with the two countries would resume after nine months.

title: Poland Beefs Up Security at Border With Russia
partialText: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said there had been “disturbing movement” in Kaliningrad, a Russian region just north of Poland.

title: Trump’s Immigration Dragnet Sweeps Up Ukrainian Truckers Who Fled War
partialText: At least a dozen Ukrainian truck drivers were arrested this summer, according to a representative for Ukraine. Several remain in detention.

title: Supreme Court to Hear Catholic Schools’ Challenge to Colorado Aid Rules
partialText: The Supreme Court considered whether Catholic preschools in Colorado that decline to enroll families with gay and transgender parents can participate in a state program.

title: Google Will Turn Off Search for Schools That Reject A.I.
partialText: Google is making it easier to restrict its A.I. tools for students. But schools that block A.I. entirely will lose student access to Google’s search engine.

title: Ken Burns: Why I’m Optimistic About the Midterms
partialText: There’s something fundamental at stake in the midterms this year, beyond policy differences.

title: Five Telltale Signs of a Democratic Blowout
partialText: The political winds are blowing in Democrats’ direction. The question is: How strong are they?

title: House Republicans Accuse Top Psychology Group of Antisemitism
partialText: A monthslong G.O.P. effort culminated in a scathing report about emails and other exchanges within the American Psychological Association.
